surfaces.part: ramp surface (peat ground with step/tread lines)

answer.evidence: The tile is a full 32-wide olive peat surface from row 0 to 31, seen from above. Thin darker lines at rows 11-12, 19 and 24 are step or tread edges across the ramp. Their risers face away from the viewer, so there is no south-facing vertical face. Dark wedges at the left and right edges (from about row 8, widening toward rows 18-31) are the cut cliff walls beside the ramp, not a front face. Column scans at x=8, 16 and 23 show only small lightness changes, with no front-edge line, eave shadow or ellipse. The ramp reads as a flat top-down slab with no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate reads as a few horizontal olive-yellow bands with a dark rim, like stacked slabs, and shows little peat grain or per-clump variation. Only 11 distinct colours across the whole patch gives about 4 usable ramp steps against 5-6 in the references. The measured 7 visible tones per tile matches the paving reference and beats the grass reference (3), but those tones come from the banding rather than from surface texture. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large single-colour areas by the numbers, though by eye the bands look smooth. 57% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is mixed: partly tinted, partly near-black, which leans toward the sticker look rather than the dark-material-tone edges of the references. A cut-through peat cliff should show crumbly soil grain, root flecks and tonal breakup along the face, and this piece looks thinner and flatter than the references. When in doubt, fail.
